flags: ODOT describes an 80-mile tour route, not the catalog’s mapped 106.8-mile corridor. Catalog strip order places Cove before Union and Medical Springs; ODOT’s itinerary and current story place Hot Lake first, Medical Springs on the southern loop, and Cove afterward. Draft follows the authoritative cached itinerary; reconcile the app map before publication.

ODOT calls Hot Lake ruins, while the hotel history documents restoration from 2003 and further work after 2020. Draft uses the dated restoration history and makes no current lodging or bathing-access promise.

No tour-route designation date, road builders or campaign history are cached. History explains earlier travel and the documented effect of highway construction without calling the Oregon Trail the modern tour route.
Hot Lake is retained as a documented National Register landmark, not as a business recommendation. Medical Springs’ former resort is treated as community history.

Medical Springs access evidence is dated 2022 and says the pool is closed to the public; no bathing visit is suggested. The claimed causal link to the Pondosa mill fire conflicts with the neighboring town’s chronology, so it is omitted.
Practical checked date records review of the saved ODOT text, not live road-condition verification.
